The QwenGyre elastic RL framework was used on Qwen’s […] The post Alibaba Qwen Introduces QwenGyre: Elastic Reinforcement Learning RL for XLong-Horizon Agents appeared first on MarkTechPost . ]]> Alibaba’s Qwen team has introduced QwenGyre , an elastic reinforcement learning RL framework for extreme-long-horizon agent training. QwenGyre is an online reinforcement learning system from Alibaba that trains coding agents through unmodified, black-box harnesses. It targets rollouts that run for hours and process close to 1M tokens. The QwenGyre elastic RL framework was used on Qwen’s flagship Qwen 3.8 2.4T model. It rests on 2 core ideas. It moves idle GPUs between rollout and training. It also turns branching agent histories into bounded training samples. TL;DR Size: A training framework, not a model. Tested on Qwen 3.6 122B and Qwen 3.8 2.4T ( A95B per Qwen ), with ~700K tokens per rollout. Runs on: Multi-node GPU clusters. The 122B runs used 24 to 32 nodes; the 2.4T run used 192 nodes (4 cells of 48). GPU model not disclosed. Megatron trains, SGLang serves rollouts. Performance: 1.38x to 1.78x faster than Async, 1.21x to 1.85x faster than Colocate, at matched scores. Best: 1.85x end-to-end speedup over Colocate on TerminalBench. Worst: Only 1.21x over Colocate on the 2.4T model, where many queries ran near the timeout. Bottom line: Best: NL2RepoBench rises from 52.5% to 58.5% in 48 steps. Worst: the paper links no public code release. What problem does QwenGyre solve? The research team defines ‘XLong-horizon’ tasks as agent runs spanning hours and hundreds of model and tool interactions. Examples include generating full repositories from specs, as in NL2Repo-Bench . Two problems appear at this scale: First, rollouts have long tails. In a Colocate setup, training waits for the slowest execution while GPUs idle. In an Async setup, fixed GPU pools cannot lend spare capacity to each other. Second, harnesses like Claude Code compact context, spawn sub-agents and retry. One execution becomes a branching tree, not a single trajectory. Expanding every path duplicates shared prefixes and inflates training cost. How does the Elastic Scheduler work? QwenGyre splits GPUs into cells that share a training layout. Each cell can serve rollouts or host a full training replica. A core cell owns the authoritative weights and optimizer state. Satellite cells join training later. The scheduler tracks a rollout waterlevel: queued and running executions. As executions finish, cells switch to training once the remaining cells can still serve all live work. Model calls are rerouted through a proxy, so the harness keeps running. Key mechanics: KV-cache blocks migrate over RDMA during rerouting, reducing prefix recomputation. Satellites pull core weights through Mooncake’s Transfer Engine and join an ongoing batch. Streaming training lets cells claim micro-steps as data becomes ready. Average role switches took 8.52 s (rollout to training) and 3.46 s (training to rollout). How does the Trajectory Processor build training samples? A proxy records exact token IDs and behavior log-probabilities using token-in, token-out (TITO) . Calls are stored as prefix-shared trajectory trees . Partial scoring: Timed-out executions are still scored on their preserved workspace. Evaluator failures are excluded, never treated as a zero reward. Bounded sampling: At most 5 trajectories per execution are kept, ranked main > main-summary > sub-agent > sub-agent-summary. Deduplication: Shared targets count once, and only policy-generated tokens are trained. Fair weighting: Losses average within each execution, so extra branches do not inflate its weight. A cap of 5 matched uncapped training scores while cutting forward-backward time by 25.2%. Training uses an adapted GSPO with 16 rollouts per group. How fast is QwenGyre? Benchmark results All runs used Claude Code 2.1.220 as the harness, with equal GPU budgets and matched staleness. Workload (model) vs Async vs Colocate NL2RepoBench (Qwen 3.6 122B, 48 steps) 1.42x to 1.53x 1.36x to 1.47x DeepSWE (Qwen 3.6 122B, 24 steps) 1.569x to 1.572x 1.610x to 1.824x TerminalBench (Qwen 3.6 122B, 24 steps) 1.383x to 1.430x 1.809x to 1.849x NL2RepoBench (Qwen 3.8 2.4T, 48 steps) 1.78x 1.21x On the 2.4T model, QwenGyre finished 48 steps in 75.42 hours. Async took 134.55 hours and Colocate took 91.47 hours. Evaluation pass rate rose from 52.48% to 58.54%. How does QwenGyre compare with other agentic RL frameworks? Key Takeaways QwenGyre moves GPUs between rollout and training without stopping live agents. Trajectory trees cap samples at 5 per execution and train shared prefixes once. Timed-out runs still get scored on their partial work. Up to 1.85x faster than Colocate and 1.78x faster than Async. Qwen 3.8 2.4T NL2RepoBench improved from 52.5% to 58.5% in 48 steps. Over 1,000 enterprise customers use Prove’s platform to process 20 billion customer requests annually across industries, including banking, lending, healthcare, gaming, crypto, e-commerce, marketplaces, and payments. For the latest updates from Prove, </span><a href="https://www.linkedin.com/company/proveidentity/"><span>follow us on LinkedIn.</span></a></p> <p><span>Prove is driving the future of digital identity. We are looking for Provers who know how to make an impact. We’re talking self-starting professionals who thrive in a fast-paced environment, process information quickly, and make intelligent decisions. The work is challenging and requires not only smart but natural curiosity and tenacity. Teamwork is also important to us – we work together and play together.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</span></p> <p><span>Prove has big plans, and we’re excited about the future. If this sounds like the place for you – come join our team!&nbsp;</span></p> </div></div><p><strong>Title:&nbsp;</strong>Senior Software Engineer</p> <p><strong>Department: </strong>Engineering</p> <p><strong>Reports To: </strong>Manager, Engineering</p> <p><strong>FLSA Status: </strong>Exempt</p> <p><strong>Location:</strong> US Remote</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h3>Job Summary</h3> <p>As a Senior Software Engineer at Prove, you will play a critical role in building, maintaining, and scaling the technology that powers the next generation of identity verification. Whether working on consumer and business identity services or developing low-level phone intelligence data signals, you will design and implement robust, high-performance solutions. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams to solve complex technical challenges, improve system architecture, and contribute to the mission-critical infrastructure that helps institutions solve fraud and verify digital identity worldwide.<br><br></p> <h3>Team Focus Areas</h3> <p>We are currently hiring for two engineering teams, each solving unique challenges in the identity space:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Data Engineering Team:</strong> Join our team to design and build the fault-tolerant, scalable platforms powering our core identity services (Verified Users, Prefill, and KYB/KYC). You’ll work hands-on with senior engineers and product leaders to tackle complex, high-scale architectural challenges and directly influence our identity verification roadmap.</li> <li><strong>Phone Number Intelligence:</strong> Our team focuses on phone intelligence and generating low-level data signals used by various internal services. This work is foundational to our fraud detection capabilities, providing specialized knowledge of mobile carrier data and fraud patterns. We are currently migrating data and migrating to an event-driven architecture, offering an exciting opportunity for someone to shape our infrastructure.</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h3>Responsibilities</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Engineering Excellence:</strong> Write high-quality, maintainable code, develop detailed technical documentation, and champion strong engineering principles within the team.</li> <li><strong>System Development:</strong> Design and develop microservices within a cloud-native, distributed architecture.</li> <li><strong>Problem Solving:</strong> Analyze, debug, and resolve production issues. Proactively engage in technical design discussions, including writing and reviewing RFCs for new solutions.</li> <li><strong>Technical Leadership:</strong> Mentor team members, participate in code reviews, and drive technical decisions. Own end-to-end features—from initial design and RFC creation to implementation and maintenance.</li> <li><strong>Collaborative development: </strong>Participate in the "Owner/Helper" project model; contribute as a lead owner for major milestones and actively support team members on their own initiatives.</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h3>Your First Three Months</h3> <p><strong>30 Days (Onboarding):</strong> Gain a high-level understanding of our architecture, team goals, and existing services. Make your first code contributions by resolving bugs or tackling small tasks within the codebase.</p> <p><strong>60 Days (Contribution):</strong> Integrate into the design process by reviewing RFCs and providing technical feedback. Contribute significantly as an active team member to one of our milestones.</p> <p><strong>90 Days (Ownership):</strong> Develop a deep grasp of our product and migration strategies. Take ownership of a minor or major milestone, or lead the drafting of an RFC for a new initiative.</p> <h3>Qualifications</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Software Development:</strong> 6+ years of professional software development experience, with a deep understanding of object-oriented programming (Java highly preferred).</li> <li><strong>System Design:</strong> Experience designing event-driven, robust, and scalable solutions for complex technical problems.</li> <li><strong>Cloud Proficiency:</strong> Hands-on experience with public cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, or Azure).</li> <li><strong>Data &amp; Database Expertise:</strong> Proficiency in SQL (Oracle) and NoSQL (DynamoDB) with strong knowledge of design principles for both.</li> <li><strong>Education:</strong> Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, a quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience.</li> </ul> <h3>Preferred Qualifications</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Full-Stack Development:</strong> Experience with TypeScript and React.</li> <li><strong>CI/CD &amp; Testing:</strong> Ability to build automated test frameworks and CI/CD pipelines.</li> <li><strong>Streaming Technologies:</strong> Practical experience with Kafka and Flink.</li> <li><strong>Modern Tech:</strong> Familiarity with AI and machine learning integrations.</li> <li><strong>Technical Leadership:</strong> Proven ability to influence team direction and long-term architectural decisions.</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p>This position description should not be considered the final description of the position. QwenGyre is an online reinforcement learning system from Alibaba that trains coding agents through unmodified, black-box harnesses. It targets rollouts that run for hours and process close to 1M tokens. The QwenGyre elastic RL framework was used on Qwen’s flagship Qwen 3.8 2.4T model. It rests on 2 core ideas. It moves idle GPUs between rollout and training. It also turns branching agent histories into bounded training samples. TL;DR Size: A training framework, not a model. Tested on Qwen 3.6 122B and Qwen 3.8 2.4T ( A95B per Qwen ), with ~700K tokens per rollout. Runs on: Multi-node GPU clusters. The 122B runs used 24 to 32 nodes; the 2.4T run used 192 nodes (4 cells of 48). GPU model not disclosed. Megatron trains, SGLang serves rollouts. Performance: 1.38x to 1.78x faster than Async, 1.21x to 1.85x faster than Colocate, at matched scores. Best: 1.85x end-to-end speedup over Colocate on TerminalBench. Worst: Only 1.21x over Colocate on the 2.4T model, where many queries ran near the timeout. Bottom line: Best: NL2RepoBench rises from 52.5% to 58.5% in 48 steps. Worst: the paper links no public code release. What problem does QwenGyre solve? The research team defines ‘XLong-horizon’ tasks as agent runs spanning hours and hundreds of model and tool interactions. Examples include generating full repositories from specs, as in NL2Repo-Bench . Two problems appear at this scale: First, rollouts have long tails. In a Colocate setup, training waits for the slowest execution while GPUs idle. In an Async setup, fixed GPU pools cannot lend spare capacity to each other. Second, harnesses like Claude Code compact context, spawn sub-agents and retry. One execution becomes a branching tree, not a single trajectory. Expanding every path duplicates shared prefixes and inflates training cost. How does the Elastic Scheduler work? QwenGyre splits GPUs into cells that share a training layout. Each cell can serve rollouts or host a full training replica. A core cell owns the authoritative weights and optimizer state. Satellite cells join training later. The scheduler tracks a rollout waterlevel: queued and running executions. As executions finish, cells switch to training once the remaining cells can still serve all live work. Model calls are rerouted through a proxy, so the harness keeps running. Key mechanics: KV-cache blocks migrate over RDMA during rerouting, reducing prefix recomputation. Satellites pull core weights through Mooncake’s Transfer Engine and join an ongoing batch. Streaming training lets cells claim micro-steps as data becomes ready. Average role switches took 8.52 s (rollout to training) and 3.46 s (training to rollout). How does the Trajectory Processor build training samples? A proxy records exact token IDs and behavior log-probabilities using token-in, token-out (TITO) . Calls are stored as prefix-shared trajectory trees . Partial scoring: Timed-out executions are still scored on their preserved workspace. Evaluator failures are excluded, never treated as a zero reward. Bounded sampling: At most 5 trajectories per execution are kept, ranked main > main-summary > sub-agent > sub-agent-summary. Deduplication: Shared targets count once, and only policy-generated tokens are trained. Fair weighting: Losses average within each execution, so extra branches do not inflate its weight. A cap of 5 matched uncapped training scores while cutting forward-backward time by 25.2%. Training uses an adapted GSPO with 16 rollouts per group. How fast is QwenGyre? Benchmark results All runs used Claude Code 2.1.220 as the harness, with equal GPU budgets and matched staleness. Async took 134.55 hours and Colocate took 91.47 hours. Evaluation pass rate rose from 52.48% to 58.54%. How does QwenGyre compare with other agentic RL frameworks? The post Z.ai GLM-Legal Beats Claude Fable 5 and Kimi K3 on Harvey LAB appeared first on MarkTechPost . ]]> Z.ai just released GLM-Legal . GLM-Legal is a legal AI model from Z.ai, built on GLM-5.3-Flash and trained for agentic legal work. It targets contract review, evidence analysis and compliance research. The key result is a 19.2% all-pass rate on Harvey’s Legal Agent Benchmark (LAB) . That is nearly 3x its base model’s 6.7%. For developers, the catch is access: the API is application-only for now. TL;DR Size: Built on GLM-5.3-Flash, a 320B-total, 18B-active MoE with a 1M-token context and 128K max output. Z.ai lists no separate GLM-Legal parameter count. Runs on: Z.ai’s hosted API only, by application. No public weights. The base model self-hosts on multi-GPU servers via vLLM or SGLang, with FP8 weights. Performance: Top-10 on Harvey LAB at a fraction of frontier cost. Within 2.3 points of the LegalBench leader. Best: 19.17% Harvey LAB task pass rate, #7 of 79 on Vals AI, at $0.15 per test. Worst: 41.83% on Vals AI’s Legal Research Bench, below its own base model (45.19%). Bottom line: Best: frontier-class legal agent scores at about 1/128 the cost of Claude Fable 5. Worst: gated beta with no price, no weights and slow runs (1h12m per task). What is GLM-Legal? GLM-Legal is a domain-specialized version of GLM-5.3-Flash for law firms, in-house counsel and compliance teams. The base is Z.ai’s first natively multimodal GLM-5 model . It has 320B total parameters with 18B active. It mixes sparse and linear attention to cut long-context serving cost. It reads text, images, video and files, and outputs text. How was GLM-Legal trained? Training ran in 2 stages: Mid-training on expanded legal corpora, to strengthen reasoning from facts to rules to conclusions. Post-training with reinforcement learning across tens of thousands of legal task environments . The Z.ai team also describes the agent harness co-evolving with the model during post-training. Edge cases in training exposed harness bottlenecks. Harness fixes then exposed the model to more realistic constraints. How does GLM-Legal score on Harvey’s Legal Agent Benchmark? Harvey LAB is an open-source benchmark of 1,250 tasks across 24 practice areas . Over 75,000 expert-written rubric criteria grade the work. A task passes only if every criterion passes. Harvey calls this all-pass grading. Vals AI runs the held-out set with 2 LLM judges and internet disabled . Agents get file tools plus docx , pptx and xlsx skills. On that leaderboard, GLM-Legal scores 19.17% and ranks #7 of 79. Its base, GLM-5.3-Flash, scores 6.67%. The 12.5-point lift is the core claim, and an independent evaluator reproduced it. Z.ai’s launch chart shows GLM-Legal ahead of Kimi K3 (12.92%), Claude Fable 5 (11.25%) and GPT-6 Astra (5.42%). Those figures match Vals AI. The chart omits 6 models ranked higher, led by Muse Spark 1.2 at 25.42%. GLM-Legal also passes 92.5% of individual criteria. Top models sit near 90% to 95% on that measure. Does GLM-Legal match frontier models on LegalBench? Roughly. Z.ai claims parity on LegalBench and the Chinese-focused PLawBench without publishing numbers. Vals AI scores GLM-Legal at 86.23% on LegalBench . Claude Fable 5 leads at 88.56% . Kimi K3 scores 86.21% . How does GLM-Legal compare with Kimi K3, Claude Fable 5 and GPT-6 Astra? You should have. Over the past decade, Tosin and his team built Moniepoint into the operating system for more than 6 million Nigerian businesses, processing over $300 billion a year , or 39% of Nigeria’s digital payments volume and 8 out of every 10 in-person payments . As a Nigerian American, I’ve witnessed my father make trips to Western Union to send money back home for decades, and I experienced Nigeria’s fee-laden payment system when visiting the country. Moniepoint is transforming that system. Nnamdi Okike, co-founder and managing partner of 645 Ventures. Moniepoint is not alone. Sea Limited , Grab , Kaspi , Yassir , Nubank 1 — these are companies most Americans have never heard of, despite them being worth several tens or hundreds of billions, following the trail blazed by Tencent , Alibaba and MercadoLibre . These are super apps that bundle banking, commerce, ride-hailing and bill pay into one trusted application. The idea never took hold in the U.S. for one reason: trust is cheap here. With 96% of households already banked , a specialist app inherits the credibility of the financial system. Where trust is cheap, there is no need for a super app. Build trust first In emerging markets, trust is the whole problem. Four conditions tend to precede a super app: High mobile penetration, which makes distribution cheap; weak incumbent competition; poor existing financial services; and the condition most investors screen past, a financial crisis severe enough to strip incumbents of legitimacy. These populations are not merely underbanked. They were harmed, and the institutions that harmed them still hold the market. Brazil froze roughly 80% of bank deposits and financial investments for 18 months in 1990 in an effort to break hyperinflation. The banking consolidation that followed left five banks holding about 80% of banking assets and charging card rates north of 300% . That was the void Nubank was born into. Kazakhstan went through it twice: savings erased by inflation in the thousands of percent when the ruble zone collapsed in 1993, then a 2007–09 banking crisis in which the country’s largest bank, BTA, holding roughly a quarter of the system’s assets, was nationalized and defaulted amid allegations of multibillion-dollar fraud. Kaspi grew into that void. Southeast Asia’s 1997 crisis was harsher still. Indonesia closed 16 banks in a single announcement, the rupiah lost about 85% of its value, and output fell 13 %. Two decades later roughly half of Indonesian adults still had no bank account, which enabled Sea to build Shopee and SeaMoney into that gap. Kaspi also answers the objection I hear most from American investors, which is that these markets are too small to produce large exits. Kazakhstan has only 20 million people, and according to company filings , around 14 million — nearly 70% of its population — use Kaspi. The average user transacts roughly 77 times a month . It earns $9 billion of revenue at 56% EBITDA margins, and its enterprise value is over $17 billion . Depth of spend, not population, sets the ceiling. Compare Nubank to Chime . Nubank has 14x the customers, 127 million to Chime’s 9.5 million , about 7x the revenue and a market capitalization more than 6x larger. Nubank has brought over 31 million previously unbanked Brazilians into the financial system . A technology applied in an overlooked market with a large unaddressed pain point can build a bigger and more defensible company than the same technology applied in a rich one. Screen for the four conditions and a few markets stand out as places where the next super app could emerge: Bangladesh: Five banks looted from the inside for years before the 2024 change in government exposed them , with the government now promising to pay 7.5 million savers whose money is gone. Egypt: Repeated devaluations of the pound between 2016 and 2024, shrinking savings held at banks the state itself owns. Vietnam: Savers pulled 80% of deposits out of one major bank in 2022 after its owner was arrested in a $24 billion fraud. Pakistan: A near-default and 38% inflation in 2023 , then government-built rails and a national ID that makes onboarding nearly costless. One boundary condition: The crisis must be severe enough to delegitimize incumbents but contained enough that the currency and payment rails still work. The first generation of super apps created enormous value for the investors who backed them early. In 2001, the South African media company Naspers paid roughly $34 million for a 46.5% stake in Tencent, a stake later worth more than $100 billion and one of the best tech investments ever made . Sequoia Capital ’s investment in Nubank’s $2 million seed round, combined with its lead Series A investment, was worth $7 billion at the company’s IPO . The second generation is scaling now. The third will be built on stablecoins and AI technologies, in Abidjan, Buenos Aires, Karachi and Lagos, by founders like Tosin Eniolorunda who will play an increasingly important role in the growth of emerging market economies. Nnamdi Okike is co-founder and managing partner of 645 Ventures , where he oversees the firm’s investing strategy, governance and compliance, with a focus on fintech and enterprise technology. Since co-founding 645 Ventures in 2014, he has invested in and partnered with companies including RentSpree , Setpoint , Sequence , Solidus Labs , Order and Uptiq . Previously, he was an investor at Insight Partners , where he invested in 19 companies and had nine exits representing more than $9 billion in exit value. Prove’s phone-centric identity tokenization and passive cryptographic authentication solutions reduce friction, enhance security and privacy across all digital channels, and accelerate revenues while reducing operating expenses and fraud losses. Over 1,000 enterprise customers use Prove’s platform to process 20 billion customer requests annually across industries, including banking, lending, healthcare, gaming, crypto, e-commerce, marketplaces, and payments. For the latest updates from Prove, </span><a href="https://www.linkedin.com/company/proveidentity/"><span>follow us on LinkedIn.</span></a></p> <p><span>Prove is driving the future of digital identity. We are looking for Provers who know how to make an impact. We’re talking self-starting professionals who thrive in a fast-paced environment, process information quickly, and make intelligent decisions. The work is challenging and requires not only smart but natural curiosity and tenacity. Teamwork is also important to us – we work together and play together.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</span></p> <p><span>Prove has big plans, and we’re excited about the future. If this sounds like the place for you – come join our team!&nbsp;</span></p> </div></div><p><strong>Title:&nbsp;</strong>Senior Software Engineer</p> <p><strong>Department: </strong>Engineering</p> <p><strong>Reports To: </strong>Manager, Engineering</p> <p><strong>FLSA Status: </strong>Exempt</p> <p><strong>Location:</strong> US Remote</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h3>Job Summary</h3> <p>As a Senior Software Engineer at Prove, you will play a critical role in building, maintaining, and scaling the technology that powers the next generation of identity verification. Whether working on consumer and business identity services or developing low-level phone intelligence data signals, you will design and implement robust, high-performance solutions. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams to solve complex technical challenges, improve system architecture, and contribute to the mission-critical infrastructure that helps institutions solve fraud and verify digital identity worldwide.<br><br></p> <h3>Team Focus Areas</h3> <p>We are currently hiring for two engineering teams, each solving unique challenges in the identity space:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Data Engineering Team:</strong> Join our team to design and build the fault-tolerant, scalable platforms powering our core identity services (Verified Users, Prefill, and KYB/KYC). You’ll work hands-on with senior engineers and product leaders to tackle complex, high-scale architectural challenges and directly influence our identity verification roadmap.</li> <li><strong>Phone Number Intelligence:</strong> Our team focuses on phone intelligence and generating low-level data signals used by various internal services. This work is foundational to our fraud detection capabilities, providing specialized knowledge of mobile carrier data and fraud patterns. We are currently migrating data and migrating to an event-driven architecture, offering an exciting opportunity for someone to shape our infrastructure.</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h3>Responsibilities</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Engineering Excellence:</strong> Write high-quality, maintainable code, develop detailed technical documentation, and champion strong engineering principles within the team.</li> <li><strong>System Development:</strong> Design and develop microservices within a cloud-native, distributed architecture.</li> <li><strong>Problem Solving:</strong> Analyze, debug, and resolve production issues. Proactively engage in technical design discussions, including writing and reviewing RFCs for new solutions.</li> <li><strong>Technical Leadership:</strong> Mentor team members, participate in code reviews, and drive technical decisions. Own end-to-end features—from initial design and RFC creation to implementation and maintenance.</li> <li><strong>Collaborative development: </strong>Participate in the "Owner/Helper" project model; contribute as a lead owner for major milestones and actively support team members on their own initiatives.</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h3>Your First Three Months</h3> <p><strong>30 Days (Onboarding):</strong> Gain a high-level understanding of our architecture, team goals, and existing services. Make your first code contributions by resolving bugs or tackling small tasks within the codebase.</p> <p><strong>60 Days (Contribution):</strong> Integrate into the design process by reviewing RFCs and providing technical feedback. Contribute significantly as an active team member to one of our milestones.</p> <p><strong>90 Days (Ownership):</strong> Develop a deep grasp of our product and migration strategies. Take ownership of a minor or major milestone, or lead the drafting of an RFC for a new initiative.</p> <h3>Qualifications</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Software Development:</strong> 6+ years of professional software development experience, with a deep understanding of object-oriented programming (Java highly preferred).</li> <li><strong>System Design:</strong> Experience designing event-driven, robust, and scalable solutions for complex technical problems.</li> <li><strong>Cloud Proficiency:</strong> Hands-on experience with public cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, or Azure).</li> <li><strong>Data &amp; Database Expertise:</strong> Proficiency in SQL (Oracle) and NoSQL (DynamoDB) with strong knowledge of design principles for both.</li> <li><strong>Education:</strong> Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, a quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience.</li> </ul> <h3>Preferred Qualifications</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Full-Stack Development:</strong> Experience with TypeScript and React.</li> <li><strong>CI/CD &amp; Testing:</strong> Ability to build automated test frameworks and CI/CD pipelines.</li> <li><strong>Streaming Technologies:</strong> Practical experience with Kafka and Flink.</li> <li><strong>Modern Tech:</strong> Familiarity with AI and machine learning integrations.</li> <li><strong>Technical Leadership:</strong> Proven ability to influence team direction and long-term architectural decisions.</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p>This position description should not be considered the final description of the position. Kyro AI builds the software behind that effort: workforce and contractor management for electric utilities, storm restoration contractors, and aggregators. We are headquartered in Plano, Texas, and were spun off from Think Power Solutions, so we pair long-standing utility expertise with the pace and ownership of a product company.<br><br><a href="https://kyro.ai/">https://kyro.ai/</a></p> <p>WHY JOIN KYRO<br>- Work that matters: our platform helps communities get power back after storms and keeps a critical, regulated industry compliant.<br>- A growing product suite: StormShield for storm restoration, Kyro Capital for contractor invoice factoring, KORY (our AI copilot), and contractor onboarding and verification.<br>- Credibility from day one: you sell with the backing of real utility relationships and domain know-how.<br>- Close to leadership: direct access to the CEO and product team, and what you hear from customers shapes the roadmap.<br>- Room to grow: a clear path from SDR to Account Executive.<br>- Flexibility: fully remote team.</p> <p>THE ROLE<br>As an SDR, you are the first conversation most utilities and contractors have with Kyro. You will work two segments with very different buying motions:</p> <p>Utilities (enterprise): You will talk to storm response, emergency management, contractor management, supply chain, and procurement leaders. Cycles are long, involve multiple stakeholders, and are often tied to RFIs/RFPs. A win is a qualified discovery meeting or demo handed to the account team.</p> <p>Contractors (SMB to mid-market): You will talk to owners, operations managers, and storm coordinators at line, vegetation, and restoration contractors. Cycles are shorter, phone-first, and owner-led. A win is a demo held and the contractor signed up and onboarded.</p> <p>WHAT YOU'LL DO<br>- Prospect outbound: research target utilities and contractors, build account lists, and reach decision-makers by phone, email, and LinkedIn.<br>- Own the follow-up: run multi-touch cadences, chase no-shows and stalled conversations, and make sure every lead has a dated next step.<br>- Respond to inbound leads the same business day and qualify them before they go cold.<br>- Qualify with rigor: confirm need, timeline, decision process, budget, and compliance requirements before booking.<br>- Book and confirm demos, send reminders, and hand off with clear notes.<br>- Drive conversions: stay with contractors after the demo until they sign up and start onboarding; keep utility opportunities moving to the next stage.<br>- Keep the CRM clean: log every activity, stage change, and next step.<br>- Feed the product team: share objections, competitor mentions, and feature requests from the field.</p> <p>HOW SUCCESS IS MEASURED<br>Success is measured on demos held and the conversions that follow. Activity counts are leading indicators, not the goal. KPIs: demos booked, demos held, demo-to-opportunity rate, conversions (contractors signed up and onboarded; utility opportunities advanced to proposal or pilot), pipeline sourced, speed to lead, follow-up coverage (share of open leads with a dated next step), and outreach activity. Targets are set separately for each segment; utility credit weighs meetings and pipeline more than closed conversions.</p> <p>WHAT YOU BRING<br>- 1-3 years as an SDR or BDR in B2B sales, ideally SaaS, with a record of hitting or beating meeting and demo quotas<br>- Disciplined follow-up across phone, email, and LinkedIn without being reminded<br>- Confident cold calling, including with field-oriented buyers who rarely live in their inbox<br>- Clear, concise written communication<br>- Hands-on experience with a CRM and a sales engagement tool (HubSpot, Apollo, Outreach, Salesloft, or similar)<br>- Comfort with metrics: you track your own funnel and know where deals stall<br>- Ability to learn a technical, regulated domain quickly<br>- Self-directed and organized in a fully remote setting<br>- Native English speaker, available during US Central Time business hours</p> <p>NICE TO HAVE<br>- Experience selling into utilities, energy, construction, field services, or regulated industries<br>- Familiarity with storm restoration, line work, vegetation management, or contractor ecosystems<br>- Exposure to both enterprise (long-cycle) and SMB or self-serve sales motions<br>- Experience selling workforce management, compliance, or fintech products<br>- Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience</p> <p>COMPENSATION AND PROBATION<br>- Competitive market base plus uncapped commission. Base is paid bi-weekly and commission quarterly.<br>- Accelerators: 1.5x at 101-125% of quota, 2.0x above 125%.<br>- The first six months are probationary, with performance reviews at 3 and 6 months against ramped KPI targets (demos held, conversions, follow-up coverage). <br>- If targets are not met, Kyro may extend the probationary period or end employment. - - Employment remains at-will during and after probation.</p> <p>WHAT WE OFFER<br>- Competitive base and variable pay<br>- A fully remote role<br>- A clear path to Account Executive for SDRs who consistently hit target<br>- Direct exposure to product and leadership at a company shaping how utilities run storm response</p> <p><strong>To apply:</strong> <a href="https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/kyro-ai-sales-development-representative">https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/kyro-ai-sales-development-representative</a></p> Tue, 13 Oct 2026 17:13:53 +0000 Thu, 12 Nov 2026 17:13:53 +0000 https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/kyro-ai-sales-development-representative https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/kyro-ai-sales-development-representative Airbnb: Senior Manager, Quality, Volume Tiers Anywhere in the World 🇨🇦 Canada California Management and Finance Full-Time <img src="https://we-work-remotely.imgix.net/logos/0171/6567/logo.gif?ixlib=rails-4.0.0&w=50&h=50&dpr=2&fit=fill&auto=compress" /> <p> <strong>Headquarters:</strong> United States <br /><strong>URL:</strong> <a href="https://careers.airbnb.com/life-at-airbnb/">https://careers.airbnb.com/life-at-airbnb/</a> </p> <p>Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost ever
